subject: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up — post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tim Stewart <tim.stewart@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks again for the call earlier today, Tim. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on performance expectations for the private/VPC deployment: 

Recap (from our notes):
- Target P99 tail latency: 250 ms for streaming chat responses (SSE/websocket).
- Target median latency for small completion requests: <= 120 ms.
- Expected concurrency: 120 concurrent users (burst to 350 concurrent sessions during business hours).
- Sustained throughput: ~45 requests/sec average, peak ~120 req/sec.
- Token rate: typical responses ~80 tokens, peak traffic ~10k tokens/sec across the cluster.
- Streaming: you require chunked SSE support and partial tokens to reach clients within 80–120 ms after generation start.

Network / VPC-specific items we discussed:
- VPN vs. AWS Transit/Peering: ACME prefers site-to-site VPN for initial pilot, moving to VPC Peering later.
- Egress IPs & NAT: we'll provide egress IP ranges for allowlisting; confirm whether you have existing NAT gateways or need static egress.
- MTU and jumbo frames: recommended MTU 1500; if you run jumbo frames please confirm.
- Internal latency budget: RBC recommends <15 ms internal hop latency between ACME edge gateway and our private connectors for consistent P99.
- Bandwidth check: please run iperf2/3 tests between your edge and the datacenter region (we suggested us-west-2).

Action items (proposed):
1) ACME: share network diagram + egress/NAT details and firewall rules (deadline: Tue 4/20). (Sofia to attach diagram).
2) ACME: run iperf and traceroute to our provided endpoints and share results.
3) Redwood: provide static egress IP ranges and recommended MTU + tuning guide (Marissa).
4) Redwood infra: schedule a 60-min lab call to validate streaming latency and concurrency with a synthetic load (Aditya to run; target week of 4/26).

Attachments: I’m attaching a blank SLO matrix (requested-slo-matrix.xlsx) for you to confirm final numbers and a network checklist.

Next meeting: propose Tuesday 4/27 10:00 AM PT for the lab run/validation—please confirm.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment(s): requested-slo-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 34KB); redwood-network-checklist.pdf (pdf, 18KB)

From: Tim Stewart <tim.stewart@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Quick answers and notes from our side: 

- We can meet the P99 target if internal network latency is <20 ms and the egress path is stable (no more than occasional packet loss <0.1%).
- We will start with site-to-site VPN to the us-west-2 region for the pilot. Long-term, we'll evaluate VPC peering/transit.
- NAT/Egress: we use a pair of HA NAT gateways today but can allocate a pair of static egress IPs if needed. Will confirm exact addresses by Mon 4/19.
- MTU: default 1500; no jumbo frames in our current WAN.
- Concurrency and burst: the 350 concurrent session burst is valid — our product load generator typically simulates that.

Attached: initial network diagram (acme-network-diagram.pdf) and a short ops note on VPN throughput limits.

Action: Sofia will run iperf3 between our edge and the test endpoints you provide. We’ll share results by Mon 4/19.

On timing — 4/27 10AM PT works for a follow-up. For the lab run, please share ephemeral test endpoints (FQDNs) and the expected test profile (concurrency, tokens/sec) so we can coordinate load generators on our end.

—Tim
Tim Stewart
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Corp
Tim.Stewart@acme.com

Attachment(s): acme-network-diagram.pdf (pdf, 120KB); acme-vpn-notes.txt (txt, 4KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / VPC network follow-up — post-call recap & next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the diagram, Tim/Sofia — that helps a lot. A couple clarifications and next steps from our side: 

- Endpoints: we'll provide three ephemeral test IPS/FQDNs in us-west-2:
  * api-test-1.us-west-2.redwood.internal (SSE streaming endpoint)
  * api-test-2.us-west-2.redwood.internal (chunked completions endpoint)
  * iperf.us-west-2.redwood.internal (for iperf/traceroute)

- Test profile (for the lab run):
  * Baseline: 45 req/sec, 120 concurrent sessions, token rate 5k tokens/sec total.
  * Peak: 120 req/sec, 350 concurrent sessions, token rate 10k tokens/sec total.
  * Streaming validation: 80% of requests should receive first token within 120 ms, P99 of first-token latency <250 ms.

- Firewall/NAT: please ensure the following ports are open outbound from your edge: 443 (TLS API), 80 (optional for health checks), UDP 5201 for iperf3. If you need static egress IPs, we can allocate them for the pilot — let us know if ACME will use current NAT gateways or wants dedicated egress.

- Metrics we'll capture during the lab run: per-request latency histograms, token throughput, connection churn, retransmits, and packet loss. We'll also enable TCP_INFO on the connectors to correlate OS-level retransmits with higher-level latencies.

Next steps: 
1) Redwood to publish ephemeral endpoints + a brief runbook by EOD Mon 4/19 (Marissa).
2) ACME to run iperf3/traceroute + share results by Mon 4/19 (Sofia).
3) Aditya to run a preliminary internal test and validate connector settings (Aditya — can you aim for Wed 4/21 to smoke test?).
4) Full lab run 4/27 10:00 AM PT.

If those dates look good I'll lock the calendar invite and send the runbook.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks — I'll take the lead on the infra validation and test profile. Plan: 

1) Today I'll provision the ephemeral endpoints in us-west-2 and post the FQDNs + short runbook to the Drive link (expected by EOD Mon 4/19 as discussed).
2) I'll run an internal smoke test on Wed 4/21 that mimics the Baseline profile (45 req/sec, 120 concurrent). If that passes, we'll iterate to the Peak profile ahead of the lab run.
3) For streaming validation I'll instrument test harnesses to capture first-byte latency and chunk arrival times; I'll share raw histograms and a summarized P50/P95/P99.

A couple quick notes / asks for ACME: 
- When you run iperf3, please do a few long-duration runs (60s+) and save the JSON output — that'll help us look at jitter and throughput stability.
- If possible share the public egress IPs (or confirm you want Redwood static egress) — we need those for allowlisting.

I'll reply here once endpoints & runbook are posted.

—Aditya
